heroHeadline: Trump in Beijing for Xi Summit as IRGC Declares Maximum Readiness; Pentagon Eyes 'Operation Sledgehammer' WPR Reset; Brent Climbs to ~$107–108/bbl — Day 75
heroSubtitle: Day 75 (May 13): Trump arrived in Beijing for a two-day summit with Xi Jinping — Iran is expected to dominate discussions even though trade is the nominal agenda. Rubio, Hegseth, Elon Musk, Tim Cook, and Jensen Huang are accompanying him; Trump told reporters he and Xi will have a 'long talk' about Iran. NBC News reported the Pentagon is considering renaming any resumed combat operations 'Operation Sledgehammer' — a legal maneuver intended to reset the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock, sidestepping Congress without a new AUMF. IRGC Brigadier-General Mohammad Akrami Nia declared Iran's armed forces are at the 'highest level of readiness' with 'no room for retreat.' The IRGC Navy announced a vast expansion of its definition of the Strait of Hormuz — from Jask and Siri coasts extending beyond the major islands — significantly widening the area Iran claims to control. Australia confirmed it will join the UK/France-led 'strictly defensive' Hormuz shipping escort mission. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan said both sides now have 'sufficient political will' to stop the conflict. Brent crude closed May 12 at $107.77/bbl (+3.4%), holding ~$107–108/bbl on Day 75 as Saudi Aramco CEO warned 600+ tankers remain trapped with the market losing ~100M bbl/week of supply. Day 74 recap (May 12): Trump was 'more seriously thinking' of restarting combat; US imposed fresh sanctions on 12 Chinese/Iranian entities; Kuwait reported IRGC port attacks; Pentagon confirmed $29B war cost.
